note: Set B reproduces every one of Set A's millwork claims and additionally captures correct equipment, plumbing and finish facts (washing machine model/manufacturer, vinyl composite tile manufacturer/colour/dimensions, accent paint manufacturer/colour/finish, wall base material, shower valve manufacturer). However, B misbinds three values across schedule rows: STANDARD EXCELON and 51899 belong to the vinyl composite tile, not the shower valve, and T17059 is the Delta shower valve model, not a VCT model. Set A is clean but narrow, repeating three millwork rows verbatim and leaving out the equipment, plumbing and finish facts that B supplies. On balance B's larger body of correct, well-bound claims outweighs its three cross-row errors.
remarks: Both sets state each of three millwork rows twice (MWB01 vanity, MWK04 sink base cabinet, MWK05 base cabinet) - a shared redundancy pattern. The text layer scrambles the millwork rows (tags detached from descriptions, MWK01/MWK02 rows merged), so the image was needed to confirm MWK01 = BASE CABINET 2'-5 7/8" x 2'-0 7/8" x 2'-6 3/8" and MWK02 = BASE CABINET (OVEN) 2'-5 7/8" x 2'-0 3/4" x 2'-6 3/8"; A's MWK01 claim matches the image. Borderline in B: 'VINYL COMPOSITE TILE | texture | IMPERIAL TEXTURE' splits the style name 'STANDARD EXCELON IMPERIAL TEXTURE' into an attribute the page does not label; not counted as wrong but the attribute is inferred. Neither set covers MWK02, MWK03 or MWL01 millwork rows or the furniture schedule.
